sentences.text: Acuetzpalin is an extinct genus of ophthalmosaurid ichthyosaur whose name means "water lizard" in Classical Nahuatl.
The known fossil material consists of a partial skeleton that lacks limbs but features a surprisingly well-preserved skull.
Scientists estimate the animal was more than 3.1 meters long when accounting for the missing parts of the holotype — the specimen the species is based on.
The species Acuetzpalin carranzai was discovered in limestone of the La Casita Formation at Cerro de Palotes, near Cuencamé, Durango, Mexico.
Acuetzpalin is classified as a reptile in the order Ichthyosauria, suborder Neoichthyosauria, infraorder Thunnosauria, and family Ophthalmosauridae.
A 2020 phylogenetic analysis places Acuetzpalin within the subfamily Platypterygiinae among the most derived members of that group.
Fossils of Acuetzpalin come from the Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic period.
Acuetzpalin lived between 154.8 and 149.2 million years ago during the Kimmeridgian stage.
